explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem is about `unfoldDelta`, which the library defines itself at line 1516 of the same file: it maps `x :: y :: xs` to `(x - y) :: unfoldDelta (y :: xs)`, turning a list into the differences of consecutive entries. The theorem says that for a decreasing list, the sum of the i-th difference times i, counting from 1, gives back the sum of the list. This is a discrete Abel-summation identity written for that custom definition. Mathlib has nothing about `unfoldDelta`. The general Abel-summation lemmas in Mathlib (`Finset.sum_range_by_parts`) are stated with `Finset` sums and integer-style subtraction. Turning one of them into this `List`/`zipIdx` statement over truncated ℕ subtraction would take a real argument, not one or two lines of glue. The proof itself uses only routine list lemmas (`List.zipIdx_succ`, `List.sum_map_add`, `Nat.sub_eq_of_eq_add`) and the library's own `sum_unfoldDelta'`.
